take_homes: Write down what I want precisely (the gap, the job, what it reads, what it writes) and the agent builds it. Specifying is the skill, not prompt cleverness.
Make every claim cite its source file, and push back on specific lines. Ask the agent to name a critique it ignored.
Access is not uptake. Count how many folders get cited and use that as my rollout number, because my team has fourteen private copies.

monday.move: Build the skeptic agent for the usage-pricing decision from my four-line brief. Make it cite the Q2 review and flag where the churn article disagrees. Put the context files in one shared folder for the team.
monday.who: Me first, then two people from the pricing working group
monday.when: Monday morning, 25 minutes, then the working group on Tuesday
monday.stop_condition: If it can't cite a source file for each claim after two rounds of pushback, I drop it and keep the manual process
monday.blocker: No shared place for the context files; everyone keeps their own copy

misconception.why: The module says specifying well is the hard half and the shared context is what compounds. That does not fully displace my belief that prompt quality matters, but the folder-count idea made me see that the real problem is my team's setup.

one_line: The exercises are useful and the folder-counting idea was the best bit, but the closing slides repeat themselves and the 'you are now agent builders' line is too much.
